response.sql: SELECT ID, AVG(UA) AS avg_ua, AVG(HCT) AS avg_hct FROM Laboratory WHERE ID NOT IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RA = '-') GROUP BY ID ORDER BY (avg_hct IS NULL), avg_hct DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Exclusion is at the patient level: a patient is dropped if any of their lab records has RA = '-', and all of that patient's records are kept for the averages. Patients whose RA values are all NULL or other values are kept.

AVG ignores NULL UA and HCT values, as the request specifies. Patients with no non-NULL HCT get a NULL avg_hct and sort last (ORDER BY (avg_hct IS NULL) places NULLs after all numeric values in SQLite).
Ties in avg_hct are broken arbitrarily, since the request does not specify a secondary sort.

alternatives.interpretation: Drop only the individual lab records where RA = '-' and average the remaining records. A patient with some '-' records would still appear, using only their other records.
alternatives.sql: SELECT ID, AVG(UA) AS avg_ua, AVG(HCT) AS avg_hct FROM Laboratory WHERE RA IS NULL OR RA <> '-' GROUP BY ID ORDER BY (avg_hct IS NULL), avg_hct DESC LIMIT 10;
